questions.q: What is the main function of the speedometer?
options: To show the engine temperature
To show how much fuel is left
To show the current road speed in km/h
To show the total distance the car has travelled
questions.explain: The speedometer shows the current road speed in km/h, and is deliberately set to show slightly more than the true speed.

questions.q: What does the tachometer (rev counter) measure?
options: How many revolutions per minute (rpm) the engine is turning
How much fuel is left
Road speed
Coolant temperature
questions.explain: The tachometer shows rpm — the engine's rotation rate. A red zone at the top marks a range that can damage the engine.

questions.q: What is the difference between the odometer and the trip computer?
options: The odometer adds up total distance over the car's whole life; the trip computer can be reset for a single journey
The trip computer only sets service dates
The odometer shows only the current speed
There is no difference, they are the same thing
questions.explain: The odometer cannot be reset and is used to set service dates; the trip computer shows data only for the current journey.

questions.q: What is true about the speedometer in a car?
options: It is deliberately set to show slightly more than the true speed, never less
It tends to show slightly less than the true speed
It sometimes stops working at high speed
It is always perfectly accurate
questions.explain: This is a deliberate design by manufacturers, so a driver is not penalised for a slight deviation of the instrument towards too low a speed.

questions.q: What does a red light on the instrument cluster mean?
options: A sign that a system is working as normal
A reminder for a future service
A condition that needs an immediate response, not "whenever it's convenient"
General information only
questions.explain: A red light reports a condition that could cause serious damage to the car or endanger safety — and needs an immediate response.

questions.q: What does an amber (yellow) light mean?
options: You must stop the car immediately on the spot
It's always just a battery fault
The system is working as normal, no attention needed
A problem that needs attention soon, but usually does not require stopping immediately
questions.explain: An amber light marks a problem that needs attention, but you can usually carry on carefully to the nearest garage.

questions.q: What do green and blue lights on the instrument cluster indicate?
options: An urgent need for a garage visit
Low fuel level only
Always a serious fault
That a system is working as normal, not that there is a problem
questions.explain: Green and blue lights report that a system is working as expected — such as an indicator, main beam or cruise control.

questions.q: Two warning lights come on at the same time — one red, one amber. What is correct?
options: Always deal with the amber one first
Ignore both until the next service
Deal with the red one first — it is more urgent
The colour makes no difference to the order
questions.explain: Red is always the most urgent; deal with it first, even when an amber light is on at the same time.

questions.q: The low engine-oil pressure light (red) comes on. What do you do?
options: Stop immediately in a safe place and switch off the engine
Switch the engine off and on again to reset the light
Keep driving carefully until you get home
Change up a gear to reduce load on the engine
questions.explain: Low oil pressure can destroy the engine within minutes; stop immediately and switch off, rather than carrying on driving.

questions.q: What must you not do when the high engine temperature light comes on?
options: Switch off the engine
Open the radiator cap immediately while the engine is hot
Wait for the engine to cool before checking the coolant
Stop in a safe place
questions.explain: The hot coolant is boiling and under pressure; opening the cap while the engine is hot can cause severe burns.

questions.q: What is the first step when the brake system light comes on?
options: Accelerate to check whether the brakes are working
Ignore it, since it is almost always a false alarm
Check and release the handbrake
Replace the brake pads yourself immediately
questions.explain: The simple cause is usually the handbrake being on; if the light stays on after releasing it, the brake system needs checking.

questions.q: What does a lit airbag light (red) mean?
options: The battery is flat
The airbag has deployed and needs replacing
A fault in the airbag system or the seatbelt pretensioners, which could stop them working in a crash
There is no fuel in the tank
questions.explain: A lit airbag light marks a fault in the protection system itself — not it deploying. Go to a garage soon.

questions.q: The "check engine" light is flashing (not steady). What does this mean?
options: A serious misfire — slow down, avoid hard acceleration and stop soon
You should accelerate to "clean out" the engine
It only means you need to refuel
It's completely fine, you can ignore it
questions.explain: A flashing "check engine" light marks a serious misfire that could damage the catalytic converter — slow down and stop soon.

questions.q: What still works when the ABS light is on (amber)?
options: The engine stops working
The ordinary brakes keep working, but in hard braking the wheels can lock up
Nothing — the brakes don't work at all
Only the handbrake works
questions.explain: When the ABS is not active, the ordinary brake system keeps working, but without protection against wheel lock-up in hard braking.

questions.q: What do you do when the tyre pressure (TPMS) light comes on?
options: Accelerate to see if the tyre bursts
Ignore it, it's not important
Switch off the car and leave it where it is
Slow down and check the tyres soon at a filling station
questions.explain: Slow down and check the air pressure in all the tyres soon — it could be a puncture or a natural drop in pressure.

questions.q: What happens in a modern diesel engine if the AdBlue fluid runs out completely?
options: Consumption drops significantly
The engine automatically switches to petrol
There is no effect on the engine at all
In most cars, the engine will not restart until the fluid is topped up
questions.explain: In most new cars, a diesel engine with an SCR system will not restart without AdBlue fluid — it's part of the emissions requirements.

questions.q: What does the blue main beam (high beam) light indicate?
options: That there is a fault in the lights
That main beam (high beam) is currently active
That the washer fluid has run out
That cruise control is active
questions.explain: The blue light comes on while the main beam (high beam) headlights are active.

questions.q: When should you switch from main beam to dipped beam?
options: Never — main beam is always allowed
Only at low speed
Only during the day
When a vehicle approaches from the opposite direction, or when driving behind a vehicle, so as not to dazzle them
questions.explain: Main beam dazzles other drivers; switch to dipped beam when a vehicle approaches from the opposite direction or you are driving behind a vehicle.

questions.q: What does a lit cruise control light indicate?
options: That the car is in neutral
That cruise control is active and holding a constant speed
That the engine has overheated
That there is a brake fault
questions.explain: The cruise control light shows that the system is active and automatically holding the set constant speed.

questions.q: When does the service reminder light come on?
options: Only when there is a serious engine fault
Based on the distance or time since the last service — a reminder, not a fault
When the brake fluid level drops
When the fuel runs out
questions.explain: The service light is a reminder based on distance or time elapsed, not a sign of a fault — the garage resets it after the service.
